title.value: Write feedback on lesson plans with ChatGPT

introduction.value: A commenter pasted a lesson plan into ChatGPT to generate detailed feedback for a teacher, and another had it write a year 6 digital technologies lesson.

method.value: In the thread, one teacher says they pasted a relief lesson plan that was clearly written by ChatGPT back into ChatGPT and asked it to generate feedback, then pasted that feedback into an email to the classroom teacher. A commenter also says they used ChatGPT to draft a Year 6 digital technologies lesson about AI, then tweaked it because it was too much for a 45–50 minute class and used the AI-written reveal as the lesson’s ending hook.

outcome.value: The first teacher says the feedback was accurate and useful, though wordy, and the classroom teacher appreciated the detailed email. The Year 6 lesson commenter says ChatGPT was good as a starting point, but still needed edits and could not be relied on for class-specific differentiation or correct resources.

notes.value: One commenter’s practical method was to treat ChatGPT as a time-saving first draft, then trim and adapt it to the class and lesson length yourself.

Write feedback on lesson plans with ChatGPT
A commenter pasted a lesson plan into ChatGPT to generate detailed feedback for a teacher, and another had it write a year 6 digital technologies lesson.
Done with
GP
ChatGPT
What they did
In the thread, one teacher says they pasted a relief lesson plan that was clearly written by ChatGPT back into ChatGPT and asked it to generate feedback, then pasted that feedback into an email to the classroom teacher. A commenter also says they used ChatGPT to draft a Year 6 digital technologies lesson about AI, then tweaked it because it was too much for a 45–50 minute class and used the AI-written reveal as the lesson’s ending hook.
How it went
The first teacher says the feedback was accurate and useful, though wordy, and the classroom teacher appreciated the detailed email. The Year 6 lesson commenter says ChatGPT was good as a starting point, but still needed edits and could not be relied on for class-specific differentiation or correct resources.
Worth knowing
One commenter’s practical method was to treat ChatGPT as a time-saving first draft, then trim and adapt it to the class and lesson length yourself.
Try it yourself
with
ChatGPT
Copy prompt
Here is a lesson plan for [subject and year level]: [paste lesson plan]. Give me detailed, constructive feedback on the learning objectives, activity flow, timing, differentiation for [student needs], and assessment. Finish with the top three changes you'd make and a revised version of the weakest section.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/AustralianTeachers/comments/1mvvgrv
